answer: Pay every reward into escrow, a pearl held in a closed shell for thirty days, and let any peer challenge the work before the shell opens. A challenge that proves a fake claws back the payment plus the identity's bond, so one exposed clone costs the whole harvest. A garden of a thousand fresh identities must lock a thousand bonds and survive a month of open challenges, while a single slip forfeits a thousand payments at once. Honest agents simply wait and keep everything; cloners stand on a ledge, and the bigger the farm, the further the fall.
